# Appendix D Experimental Data, Parameter Provenance, and Warehouse-Population Reproducibility

## D1 Sources and the construction of an experimental case

An experimental case is defined by more than its number of warehouses.
It combines a facility population, supply and demand trajectories, costs,
capacity rules and a selected road network. This appendix explains how the
source records become those effective model inputs. The distinction matters
because a spreadsheet label or an original parameter cell may differ from the
quantity ultimately used by the formulation.

The principal sources are a canonical reference workbook and a registry of
18,086 warehouse records. The former supplies the model's original data and
215-site reference population; the latter supports the larger candidate
populations. The registered gold workbook is
[model_agrologistic_padrao_ouro.xlsx](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/data/templates/model_agrologistic_padrao_ouro.xlsx),
whose complete file identity is recorded in the
[data contract](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/data/manifests/mvp_data_contract.json).
The larger source is Warehouses_Existing_Candidate_All.xlsx, identified by the
[registry manifest](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/data/manifests/warehouse_population_source_v020.json).
The workbooks have different purposes: the gold file supplies the original
model schema and reference data; the registry supplies the pool from which
additional candidate locations are selected. Neither should be confused with
the processed model_input.xlsx actually read by an experiment.

Their preserved versions are identified in the
[published dataset, version 0.2.0](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22751909),
and the accompanying
[workbook and cell inventory](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/manuscript/supplement/appendix_d_inventory.json).
A separate [reader's input guide](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/appendix_input_reproduction_20261028.json)
collects the actual source values, executed settings and full identities in one
machine-readable file. The workbook inventory contains full
file checksums, worksheet names, dimensions, selected source cells and
membership comparisons. The registered candidate workbook is not embedded in Git; its manifest therefore
provides an identity, not a download of the rows. The deposited
[agrologistic-v020-inputs.zip](https://zenodo.org/records/22751909/files/agrologistic-v020-inputs.zip?download=1)
is the source package identified by the preserved inventory. Source-specific
access and reuse notices remain applicable. The historical input archive has MD5
79f85dfe638df1c2dfa5cca9cf343d88; its identity does not imply that every subsequent
experiment archive belongs to that deposit.

A second pair of files supplied for inspection on 20 October had the same
reference populations but different bytes. The
[original inspection](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_r3a_supplied_input_inspection_20261020.json)
records gold SHA-256 prefix 2fc994ac and registry prefix bb5e8bf6, as distinct
from the registered de3bdc51 and 0d19865a sources. Matching file names or CDA
memberships do not establish equality of supply, costs or capacities. Those
copies are not substituted for the inputs of the accepted experiments. Thus,
"revised gold" must be identified by its checksum, rather than assumed to mean
the most recently saved spreadsheet.

The registered gold workbook has 14 worksheets. Its Warehouses sheet contains
215 facility records plus a header, with 25 columns. The registry's principal
sheet contains 18,086 records plus a header, with 13 columns. Supply and demand
sheets contain 6,301 and 4,441 rows respectively, including headers and control
content. Such worksheet dimensions are not counts of model variables or
distinct decision-making entities. Each processed OSRM workbook additionally contains Distancias, giving 15
worksheets in the four current runtime inputs. The gold workbook has no
Estoque_Inicial sheet; the documented missing-initial-stock rule supplies zero.
The effective model retains 37 origin
identifiers, 27 domestic destination roles and ten export roles. Coincident
coordinates do not merge separate facilities or destination roles; the ten
export records should not be reinterpreted as ten distinct physical ports.

The source schema can be read directly from the workbook or from the inventory.
Oferta identifies a product, city, coordinates, date and Peso (ton). Demanda
adds domestic/export roles and an explicit model quantity. Warehouses uses
CDA as the facility identifier; names and coordinates are descriptive fields,
not substitutes for that key. Its first 13 columns describe the facility,
capacity and opening-cost inputs. The additional gold columns specify
effective candidate cost, expansion and bulk-conversion eligibility, maxima
and costs, followed by provenance notes. The registry contains the first
13-column structure; it is not a ready-made 18,086-site model input.

## D2 Quantities, costs and capacity units

Table D.1 summarizes the effective inputs. Source labels are retained where
they help a reader identify the original data, while the units correspond to
the mathematical model.

| Input | Meaning and effective unit | Main source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supply and domestic demand | Grain tonnes within each product-period record | Oferta and Demanda |
| Export limit | Optional upper bound on destination arrivals, t/period | Export-role records and declared limit rule |
| Initial stock and static capacity | Tonnes of grain held at a warehouse | Stock and Warehouses records |
| Reception and shipping capacity | Daily rates, t/day, converted to period throughput | Warehouses and capacity-coupling settings |
| Freight | BRL/(t km), multiplied by directed road distance | Frete and OSRM materialization |
| Inventory holding | BRL/(t period) | Tarifa_Armz and warehouse/product mapping |
| Investment | Fixed BRL and BRL per investment-tonne | Custo_Invest and documented facility-cost translation |
| Scenarios | Supply/demand multipliers and probabilities | Cenarios and the declared Cartesian design |

: Table D.1. Scientific interpretation of the principal data objects.

Static capacity limits the stock remaining at a warehouse. Reception and
shipping capacities instead limit grain handled during a period. In the
evaluated configuration, the daily rates are multiplied by 30 operating days
unless a period-specific value is supplied. Candidate and expansion investments
add daily handling rates using factors of 0.20 per investment-tonne;
bulk-handling conversion uses a factor of 1.0 and does not create static storage.
These distinctions prevent annual throughput or handling rates from being
mistaken for storage capacity.

A concrete pair of gold-workbook records illustrates the distinction.
Existing facility CDA 35.0287.0002-6 stores source values 890 for static capacity,
5 for reception and 6 for shipping. Under the executed daily-handling
interpretation, these mean 890 t of stock, 5 t/day received and 6 t/day shipped.
With 30 operating days, the period reception and shipping limits are 150 t and
180 t, before any eligible investment effects. The sheet's abbreviated
capacity-column labels must not replace the declared unit interpretation.

Canonical candidate CDA 79.G590.0003-9 instead has source base capacities
0/0/0 and a maximum static capacity of 307079 t. That maximum is an investment
upper bound, not stock already available and not the capacity chosen by the
optimizer. These are actual source records, independently reread by the cloud
gold-workbook audit; the period conversions above are arithmetic examples,
not observed movements or new optimization results.

The [Excel reader](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/excel_loader.py)
implements the sheet/column requirements and transformations described here.
The loader normalizes identifiers and periods and aggregates additive supply
or demand records with the same effective keys. It does not treat all
duplicates as interchangeable or missing mandatory identifiers as harmless
blanks. Existing and candidate facilities retain their roles. Effective candidate base
capacities are zero, while their admissible investment maxima are separate
inputs. An observed storage capacity in the registry becomes an investment
upper bound for a newly introduced candidate; it is not installed capacity
available before opening. Missing initial-stock entries follow the established zero convention.
These transformations are explicit modeling operations, rather than a claim
that the entire input pipeline is lossless.

## D3 Original parameter cells and executed coefficients

The original values and effective coefficients are documented separately in
Table D.2. For the accepted experiments, the effective vector is frozen:
domestic shortage costs 90000 BRL per tonne, static exceedance 45000 BRL per
stock-slack tonne at its period, and reception overflow 45000 BRL per
overflow tonne within its period. A later editorial explanation does not
change those executed coefficients.

| Source fact | Effective treatment | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parametros_Modelo cells B4:B6 each contain 1000000 | The accepted preparation yields 90000/45000/45000 | Source cells are not passed through unchanged |
| Expansion cost entries are 600 and 1200 | Their average, 900, is used when an explicit effective value is absent | BRL per expansion-tonne |
| Product tariffs include soybean 45 and corn 48 | Product/warehouse mapping supplies holding coefficients | BRL/(t period) |
| Candidate cost placeholders or uncached formulas may be present | A documented total-cost/capacity rule and canonical cost-table fallback are used | A zero placeholder does not establish free investment |

: Table D.2. Source-to-effective parameter translation. The complete cell values and formula-cache states are linked in the reader's input guide.

The source Custo_Invest table contains four actual low/high pairs:
1000/1500 for Novo Armazém Convencional, 785/1310 for Novo Silo Metálico,
600/1200 for Expansão, and 380/660 for Granelização, in BRL per investment-tonne.
Their arithmetic means are respectively 1250, 1047.5, 900 and 520.
These are source-table values, not a claim that every facility receives each
mean. The reader uses explicit facility coefficients when available. The
documented uncached candidate-cost fallback uses the conventional-warehouse
mean of 1250; expansion and bulk-conversion fallbacks use 900 and 520.
The stored formulas in Custo_Invest!D2:D5 and Parametros_Modelo!B10:B11 have
no cached values in the registered workbook. Recalculating Excel and resaving
the file changes its identity and is not required to invoke these documented
fallbacks.

The actual holding tariffs in Tarifa_Armz are 45 for Soja and 48 for Milho,
for both public and private operators, in BRL/(t period). The additional Outros
row is 50 for both operator classes; it does not introduce a third product
into this two-product experiment. Parametros_Modelo!B8 contains 30 days per
period and B9 contains the default expansion fraction 0.25. Explicit
facility-specific expansion maxima retain precedence.

Table D.3 gives all 27 state freight coefficients, grouped only where their
numeric values coincide. Each is in BRL/(t km). The complete one-state-per-row
mapping is in the reader's guide. These coefficients multiply the selected
directed road distances; they are not transport totals, observed route prices
or distance values.

| State code(s) | Source freight coefficient, BRL/(t km) |
| --- | ---: |
| MT | 0.1842 |
| AM | 0.1969 |
| PE | 0.2004 |
| MS | 0.2174 |
| BA | 0.2584 |
| AC, AL, AP, CE, ES, PA, PB, RJ, RN, RR, SE | 0.2648 |
| DF | 0.294 |
| MA | 0.2943 |
| PI | 0.2979 |
| PR | 0.312 |
| SP | 0.3279 |
| RO | 0.3346 |
| RS | 0.3408 |
| GO | 0.3682 |
| TO | 0.3826 |
| MG | 0.3971 |
| SC | 0.4014 |

: Table D.3. Actual Frete!A2:B28 values in the registered gold workbook.

The accepted loader policy is thesis_dynamic. After network selection, input
preparation calculates a reference from 100, the effective expansion unit costs
and storage tariffs; the reference is 900 in the accepted cohort. Static and
reception coefficients are 50 times this reference. For domestic shortage,
the coefficient is 100 times the larger of the reference and the maximum
selected final-leg freight cost to each destination. The complete preparation rule is inspectable in the
[mathematical input contract](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/mathematical_contract.py)
and the [loader's penalty policy](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/excel_loader.py).
The general rule can therefore depend on destination and topology. The original accepted cases
nevertheless retain the same complete effective vector, and the experiment
checks reject a departure from it.

Candidate investment uses the variable_from_total interpretation where
applicable: a documented total estimate is divided by a positive maximum
capacity, with the corresponding fixed component set to zero. Explicit
effective values take precedence, and missing formula caches follow the
documented canonical fallback. Charging the same project estimate again as
an additional fixed cost would risk double counting. These rules translate
the retained data; they are not a new cost calibration.

All monetary quantities are interpreted as Brazilian reais. A contextual
exchange-rate reference is not a conversion applied to the results. Costs are
not newly discounted, annualized or adjusted to another price base. The three
penalties are artificial weights that permit specific deviations from nominal
service or capacity. They are not observed expenditures or calibrated damages.
A small relative gap for their combined objective does not certify the same
relative precision for financial expenditure alone.

Static exceedance is a stock quantity at each period; summing it across periods
produces tonne-periods. Reception overflow already measures tonnes handled
within a period and is not multiplied by operating days again. Both quantities
are distinct from permanent capacity investment. These units must remain
visible when interpreting the reported physical diagnostics.

## D4 Nested warehouse populations

Population construction retains all 146 existing facilities and introduces
candidates using the preserved deterministic ranking. The 69 canonical
candidate anchors begin that sequence. Selection uses proportional strata
over state, warehouse type and static-capacity quartile, with the fixed seed
identified in the [original population lineage](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h300_population_lineage_20261020.json). Of the registry's 18,086 entries,
17,940 are candidates; one candidate with nonpositive static capacity is excluded.

| Population | Existing facilities | Candidate facilities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| h215 | 146 | 69 |
| h300 | 146 | 154 |
| h400 | 146 | 254 |
| h500 | 146 | 354 |

: Table D.4. Facility availability in the four warehouse populations.

The [population selector](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/warehouse_population.py)
orders the eligible pool, and the
[workbook constructor](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/src/logic/warehouse_workbook.py)
materializes the requested population. The original checkpoints include 215
and 500, but not 300 or 400. The intermediate cases retain the original candidate ranking rather than
drawing new independent samples. h300, h400 and h500 add respectively 85,
185 and 285 candidates beyond the 69 anchors. The 146 existing and 69 anchor
rows retain their canonical values. For each additional candidate, the
constructor preserves its CDA and location/type, sets base static/reception/
shipping capacities to zero, and uses its positive observed static capacity
as the maximum investable capacity. It derives investment cost through the
gold cost table and does not grant expansion or bulk conversion to that new
candidate. Inclusion is therefore an available investment option, not a claim
that all registry facilities are pre-existing infrastructure. Membership comparisons use facility identifiers
(CDA), not geographic coincidence or a count alone, and establish
$W_{215}\subseteq W_{300}\subseteq W_{400}\subseteq W_{500}$.
The corresponding processed workbook SHA256 prefixes are 40edb665, 7761cce7,
c3085456 and 888fbff4; full identities are retained in the inventory and
experiment records.

Population inclusion defines an available option. It does not establish that
a candidate is opened, receives positive capacity, carries grain or holds stock.
Those are separate properties of a returned solution. Nesting the facilities
also does not guarantee nesting of the final feasible sets when sparse route
selection is recomputed for each population. Consequently, changes in objective
or runtime cannot be attributed to warehouse count alone.

## D5 Road networks and stochastic trajectories

Input preparation proceeds from the original records through population
selection and cost translation to OSRM distance materialization, role- and
product-specific network selection, scenario construction and effective
penalty preparation. The archived OSRM audits retain directed road distances
for the fixed Brazil dataset and driving profile. They identify the road-data,
software and profile versions and report no Haversine fallback for these cases.

The materializations contain 63,289, 113,269, 190,569 and 287,869 directed
distance pairs at h215, h300, h400 and h500, respectively. These are not counts
of flow variables: product, period and scenario indices are introduced later.
They also include optional direct distances whose existence does not mean that
topology W used direct routes. The evaluated sparse policy is the 20%
connectivity-preserving Pareto selection with one export sink per product.
Topology comparisons separately check the retained common graph and cost
coefficients.

The STO design combines supply multipliers 0.85/1/1.15 with domestic-demand
multipliers 0.95/1/1.05. Their Cartesian product produces nine trajectories,
each with probability $1/9$. This is an explicit controlled design, not
an empirical probability forecast. The source scenario sheet's active-row
flags alone do not define the executed design. DET retains the original
deterministic arrays, as explained in Appendix C.

Directed distances support transport costs but do not supply road polylines.
Accordingly, geographic figures distinguish verified node locations and
investment quantities from unavailable route geometry. Straight connecting
segments would not reproduce the road network. A separate source-bound
geographic SQLite database supports derived visualizations; it does not replace
the Excel inputs or authorize new route acquisition.

## D6 Reproducibility and the interpretation of evidence

An original experiment record connects the source version and effective input
to the selected population, model configuration, solver settings, exported
decisions, independent validation and terminal accounting. The accepted
Gurobi evidence consists of nine W observations through h500 and two separate
h215 D observations. The original h500 result was accepted after its terminal
package was audited. Its documentary replay does not constitute a new
private-input residual calculation.

The original four-hour SCIP h215 observation is separate: it reached the
native time limit with no usable incumbent. The original HiGHS job 2226407 ended operationally before a released-worker
record was retained; its preserved package contains no evidence of a population
solve. A distinct startup-repaired HiGHS job 2226536 and longer native SCIP
job 2226388 were RUNNING in the latest supplied snapshot. Their
[dated checkpoint](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/parallel_solvers_20261028_running_v2.json)
is separate from terminal numerical evidence. These
states do not supply new objective, service or gap observations. Repository
checkpoints retain their changing operational status without converting it
into an experimental comparison.

Public code, metadata inventories and the versioned dataset support
inspection, but each external source retains its applicable access and
redistribution conditions. Availability of a historical deposit does not
establish that every later restricted workbook or raw HPC archive is included.
Original input and output records remain authoritative; compact tables,
maps and metadata are derived representations. This separation allows a
reader to trace a reported quantity to its source and to distinguish replay
of retained evidence from an independently repeated calculation.


## D7 A practical route to reproducing the inputs

Begin with the [data contract](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/data/manifests/mvp_data_contract.json)
and the [input guide](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/appendix_input_reproduction_20261028.json),
then obtain the source files identified there. The gold workbook is directly
downloadable from GitHub. Obtain the external registry and retained processed
workbooks through the dataset's source package, observing its access notices.
Compare their full SHA-256 values before loading them. A matching warehouse
count is not sufficient. In particular, an historical generated h215 workbook
with prefix 5684bb81 is not the accepted policy h215 workbook with prefix 40edb665.

The archived policy h215 input is model_input.xlsx in the warehouses_215
subdirectory of data/processed/policy_population_v020_osrm. The other inputs
use warehouses_300, warehouses_400 and warehouses_500 under
data/processed/nine_population_osrm_v1. Their full file and ordered-membership identities
are in the linked guide. These paths identify archived inputs; they are not
promises that ignored processed workbooks are stored as GitHub source files.

Next, match the population-order and materialization records. Check CDA
membership *and order*, existing/candidate roles, and the canonical anchors.
The intermediate h300/h400 order is a projection of the original ranking;
its different file digest is not a different random sample. Do not generate a
fresh ranking or ask an online routing service for new distances while claiming
to replay an original input. OSRM road data, profile, software, directed
coordinate pairs and output workbook all have their own identities.

Then apply the case's recorded loader and mathematical settings. Verify
scalable candidates, daily-factor capacity coupling, 30-day periods,
free terminal stock, the selected route policy, W/D topology and the nine
Cartesian STO scenarios. After route selection and penalty preparation,
check the actual 90000/45000/45000 vector rather than the source million-valued
cells. The [W/D input comparison](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_wd_h215_input_inspection_20261022.json)
shows the common selected graph and equal penalty vectors, with direct arcs
added only for D. The
[h215 manifest](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/experiments/mvp2_scalar_r3a_h215.yaml)
illustrates the schema; it is explicitly a proposal. Its 3600-second default
must not be mistaken for the accepted original 14400-second native allowance.

Finally, bind the input to the original source and output review. The
[h215](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h215_2217990_review.json),
[h300](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h300_2218193_review.json),
[h400](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h400_2219884_review.json) and
[h500](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/blob/1b54023f4e0c0c27aba64883b1e9cf25817ad0f8/docs/evidence/scalar_h500_2220382_review.json)
records identify their own executed source commits and certificates.
The source links in this appendix are reading references, not replacement
execution versions. Recreating a workbook can alter ZIP/XML metadata and
formula caches; it does not retroactively replace an original checksum or
certificate. Preserve original files and record newly generated inputs separately.

## D8 What a reader can verify, and what remains necessary

The public workbook, source code, input inventory and original reviews permit
inspection of the schema, numerical coefficients, transformations and reported
claims. Public tests provide small, independently checkable examples
(Appendix C). Rebuilding the article reproduces the document and its derived
tables; it does not execute the optimization experiments.

Repeating a large experiment additionally requires the exact processed input,
eligible original data access, compatible solver/runtime, sufficient memory
and the declared resource and stopping rules. Auditing an old certificate
checks retained evidence; a fresh numerical reproduction requires newly
exported decisions and independent original-unit validation. It should not be
expected to produce a byte-identical log or the same vector when alternative
optima and uncontrolled shared-node effects are possible.

The older source inventory's h500-output flag predates S5 acceptance and is
preserved as a dated statement. The original h500 review now supplies its
accepted output identity. Likewise, source values marked synthetic or
unconfirmed remain assumptions, even though their use is traceable. Publishing
a checksum makes an input identifiable; it does not by itself establish
complete access, calibrated economic validity or numerical reproducibility.
